name: General Residence Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Foreigners staying to reside (rather than visit) must hold a residency visa granted by the competent authority, register their place of residence, and pay an annual residency fee (reported at 500 Libyan dinars per individual, capped at 1,500 dinars per family) plus a residence-permit fee (100 dinars per individual) on grant or renewal, collected by the Department of Passports, Nationality and Foreigners' Affairs. This dataset found NO tiered residence-card ladder comparable to Cameroon's 2-year/10-year cards or Congo-Brazzaville's 1-year/3-year/5-year system -- validity length is described only as set case-by-case 'by the competent authority,' not as a fixed numeric progression.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a residency visa, register your place of residence, and pay the applicable annual fees.

evidence_required.document: Health insurance enrollment (mandatory for all residents)

outcome.duration_length: set case-by-case by the competent authority; no fixed multi-year ladder confirmed

sources.title: ICMPD -- The Legal Guide for Foreigners in Libya (January 2020): residency visa categories, registration duty, annual and permit fees, mandatory health insurance and social security

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Libya). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier 2, an intergovernmental organization's legal guide; no Libyan government domain could be confirmed or fetched, and given the country's fragmented governance since 2014 it is unclear whether a single authoritative government portal for this even exists nationwide. GENUINE, DISCLOSED STRUCTURAL ABSENCE: unlike Cameroon's explicit 2-tier ladder or Congo-Brazzaville's 3-tier ladder (both built earlier in this dataset), Libya's residence-permit system as documented has no confirmed fixed-duration progression -- validity is set at the discretion of the competent authority. Non-Libyan residents must also enroll in mandatory health insurance and may access social security 'within the limits set by regulations,' a real but vaguely bounded entitlement disclosed rather than overstated.
